A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HGM research project. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, mesh reconstruction and component-ablation results on THuman2.0 and HuMMan, with additional qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original rendering, reconstruction and ablation results, including CustomHumans evaluations and additional appendix comparisons.

M1.justification: v1's branch predicting Gaussians from projected SMPL features is replaced by SMPL-X vertex tokens, cross-attention and residual updates to image Gaussians. v2 introduces iterative SMPL-X parameter refinement through mask/normal matching and mesh optimization using normal and Laplacian losses. Back-view refinement also changes from the stated ControlNet-tile setup to explicitly trained ControlNet refinement with a frozen diffusion backbone.

E1.justification: Alongside retained THuman2.0, HuMMan and in-the-wild coverage, v2 adds quantitative cross-dataset evaluation on CustomHumans, including loose clothing and challenging poses. Appendix Figure 11 additionally presents THuman2.1 mesh examples, and Figures 12–14 expand targeted clothing and extreme-pose coverage. Cross-dataset evaluation itself already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: The THuman2.0 NVS comparison changes from PIFu, Impersonator++, TEXture, Magic123, S3F, HumanSGD and SIFU in v1 Table 3 to SiTH, LGM, SV3D and SIFU in v2 Table 1. The mesh comparison retains ECON/SIFU, adds SiTH and removes PIFu, PaMIR, ICON, D-IF and GTA. PIFu remains in v2's qualitative appendix comparisons. HuMMan's NVS comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v1 reports both ground-truth-SMPL and estimated-SMPL NVS variants; v2 removes the ground-truth variant and specifies testing all methods without ground-truth SMPL-X. Mesh evaluation replaces L2 normal-map error with Normal Consistency. v2 also introduces a 45-scan CustomHumans evaluation protocol and specifies fine-tuning its new LGM comparator on the same training data.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 adds an ablation removing SMPL-X refinement and extends component ablations from rendering metrics to Chamfer, P2S and Normal Consistency. Figure 10 examines initial versus refined body geometry and side-view masks; Figures 12–14 add targeted clothing and pose comparisons. The visual guidance ablation from v1 Figure 7 is retained as v2 Figure 8, rather than constituting new evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Quantitative results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: The THuman2.0 reconstruction and ablation results are substantially revised, and CustomHumans results are added, including HGM's 23.84 PSNR, 0.944 SSIM and 0.0514 LPIPS in v2 Table 1. HuMMan HGM PSNR remains 23.86, while LPIPS changes from 0.062 to 0.0591. v1's rendering-speed table is removed; v2 reports different speeds in Section 4.4. Method and protocol changes limit direct performance comparisons across versions.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the SMPL-X mask/normal optimization objective and ControlNet denoising objective in Equations 3–4. The HGM reconstruction loss remains equivalent. These are limited additions to the formal optimization formulation; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes being the first generalizable feed-forward human Gaussian framework and achieving superior novel-view synthesis. v2 removes that explicit priority claim, elevates structural SMPL-X tokens and iterative body-parameter correction to central contributions, and broadens its abstract and conclusion to claim state-of-the-art surface reconstruction as well as rendering.

C2.justification: v1 attributes tolerance of SMPL errors to implicit feature-volume guidance; v2 emphasizes iterative correction and semantically anchored vertex tokens. Its new discussion explains the advantage of side-view supervision over previous front-view alignment. Limitations change substantively: v1 identifies noisy, unregularized meshes and non-end-to-end extraction, whereas v2's appendix identifies poor hands and faces and proposes regional diffusion refinement.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents 500 training scans, 12 rendering cameras, ground-truth SMPL-X inputs during training, a negative diffusion prompt, side-mask updates every 10 fitting iterations, 200 mesh-optimization iterations and reconstruction/extraction timings. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. The estimator changes from SMPLER to PIXIE, and the repository link becomes a project-page link. v1's explicit sampling strength, sampling-step count and U-Net initialization disclosure disappear.

R1.justification: The three related-work strands remain, with focused new positioning around SMPL-X estimation failures and correction relative to ECON/SIFU. References add PIXIE, CustomHumans, SV3D, DreamAvatar and DreamGaussian, while removing works associated with discarded components or comparisons, including SMPLER, Magic123, TEXture and D-IF. Publication updates to retained works do not constitute new citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, method explanation and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Section 3.3 gains separate model and refinement subsections, the reconstruction loss moves into Section 3.5, and a discussion section is added. Limitations move to the appendix, the broader-impact paragraph disappears, and authorship information changes.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the architecture diagram, adds refinement diagrams and comparative mesh visualizations, and restructures tables to display multiple datasets and both rendering and geometry ablations. The speed table disappears, and substantial appendix comparison panels are added. Retained v1 Figures 3, 4 and 7 become v2 Figures 4, 9 and 8 respectively, with relocation or display changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for its central robustness claims through a direct refinement ablation covering rendering and geometry, quantitative CustomHumans generalization tests, and targeted clothing/pose comparisons. It also addresses v1's acknowledged lack of surface regularization and supplies important implementation details. These gains outweigh narrower baseline coverage and remaining reporting weaknesses: the broad mesh-superiority claim overlooks SIFU's better THuman2.0 Chamfer score in Table 3, and the main-versus-ablation LPIPS decimal inconsistency persists.
